$comment:
Two notes, both about things a reader will want to change.

**The icon is shared with Ping display, on purpose.** The two mods are the same corner of the product — which server, and how far away it feels — and a glyph that says "the network" says it correctly for both. There is precedent one row up: `compass` is shared by Coordinates and Direction, two readings of one thing. `MOD_ICONS` is `Record<ModId, IconName>` and not a bijection, so the sharing costs nothing structurally; what it costs is distinguishability in the Mods grid, and the answer to that is the label under the tile, which is what the grid is actually read by.

**One setting is the honest number, not an oversight.** The `server` event carries a hostname without a port and a connected flag, and `style` is the only choice that hostname supports; the shared HUD block still gives this mod `on`, `scale`, `opacity`, `background`, `border` and `padding`. There is deliberately no `hide_offline`: the chip has nothing to print in singleplayer or at the menu (`host` is the empty string on disconnect), so it draws nothing there **unconditionally**. That is behaviour, not a preference — `design/quiet-cell-system.md` puts position, scale, opacity, density, what is shown and format on the customisation side of its line, and "the widget is not there" is none of them — and a switch whose entire content is absence has no preview to move, so it would need a `NOT_IN_THE_PREVIEW` exemption from `packages/ingame/test/preview.test.tsx`, whose own doc comment calls that list the one place the gate can quietly erode. `combo` and `item_counter` carry the same note for the same reason. Do not add a second setting to make this file look fuller.
label: Server address
description: The host you are actually connected to.
settings_description: Settings for the Server address HUD mod. Reads `host` from the `server` bridge event, which is pushed on connect and on disconnect and carries an empty string on the way out — so "not connected" is a state this mod can see, and the chip simply draws nothing in it rather than offering a switch about it. `ping.show_host` is deliberately kept alongside this mod: that is the inline form, a shortened host printed after the latency figure, and this is the standalone one a player places on its own — the same split Coordinates and Direction already make between a suffix and a chip. Neither reads the other's settings. One setting is all a hostname supports; the file's `$comment` says why that is the honest count.

style.description: How much of the host is printed. `short` keeps the part players actually say out loud — `hypixel` out of `mc.hypixel.net` — and is the default because on a chip the leading `mc.` and the trailing `.net` are the two pieces that never differ between the servers a player switches between, so they cost width and carry no information. `full` prints the address exactly as it was connected to, which is what you want on a network with several proxies, on a bare IP, or in a screenshot that has to be reproducible by somebody else.
